description: What each package here is qualified against, and how an unqualified host is refused or disclosed (#11). A range is qualified only because CI installs both of its endpoints from the registry on every push and pull request (range-endpoints, python-range-endpoints) and runs the real-host tests listed under qualifiedBy against them. `npm run compat:check` fails when this record, the package manifests, and CI disagree. Endpoints are the versions the range resolved to on endpointsResolvedAt; `npm run compat:check -- --resolve` re-resolves them.

packages.name: @redact-secret/adapter-mcp
lifecycle: the core's mcp-boundary conformance fixture and runner, vendored at a pinned core commit, replayed through the public API on the real core before and after initialize()

resources/read (redact-secret/redact-secret#843): the core's mcp-resources-read fixture and runner, vendored at the same pinned core commit, replayed through the public API before and after initialize(), and carried by real SDK 1.x and 2.x clients and servers over stdio and Streamable HTTP at both endpoints of each line: host placement around client.readResource, and wrapResourceReadHandler on the low-level Server and McpServer.registerResource (fixed URI and URI template) sending exactly the fixed JSON-RPC error
opt-in argument sanitation before dispatch: a blocked argument set never reaches the server
server wrappers on the low-level Server and McpServer.registerTool: a throwing handler caught before the SDK converts its message
cancellation over the wire: the host delivers nothing, the server closes its producer and sends no response
a host that logs, persists and builds model context only from the boundary's output, including a real subprocess producer: split, block, limit, cancellation
failing onAudit and onFinding callbacks, a JSON-RPC error, and a core that fails to initialize

unqualified.how: peerDependencies pino ^10.0.0: npm 7 and later stop with ERESOLVE (checked 2026-09-25 with npm 11.4.1: adapter-pino@0.1.0 with pino@9 fails) unless --legacy-peer-deps or --force overrides it

peerDependencies ^2.0.0: npm 7 and later stop with ERESOLVE (checked 2026-09-25 with npm 11.4.1: adapter-otel@0.1.0 with sdk-trace-base@1 fails) unless --legacy-peer-deps or --force overrides it; adapter-otel-trace declares the same range

unqualified.host: OpenTelemetry JS Logs (@opentelemetry/sdk-logs, LogRecord) through the span packages
unqualified.how: adapter-otel-trace and adapter-otel are span processors: a LogRecord never passes through them. Their READMEs, and the repository README, say that OpenTelemetry Logs are not protected by them. @redact-secret/adapter-otel-logs is the separate Logs package (#178); it is unreleased (private, absent from the release plan), so nothing installable from npm protects Logs yet

peerDependencies >=0.200.0 <=0.222.0 on adapter-otel-logs, an explicit span because the SDK is 0.x (a caret on 0.200.0 admits one minor): npm 7 and later stop with ERESOLVE unless --legacy-peer-deps or --force overrides it. The cap is the highest tested release: a newer one is unqualified until it is added as an endpoint here. Releases between the two endpoints are inside the range and not exercised individually

unqualified.host: OpenTelemetry Logs content outside the log record's own fields (adapter-otel-logs)
unqualified.how: packages/adapter-otel-logs/README.md names what is not covered: the resource, the instrumentation scope, attribute and map keys, ids, timestamps and severity number, a processor registered ahead of the wrapper (the SDK shares one record object in registration order), and spans and metrics

unqualified.host: Core WebAssembly fallback (artifact() === "wasm") outside the Linux x64 omit-optional lane
unqualified.how: docs/compatibility.md (Platforms and artifacts): the fallback is exercised on Linux x64, Node 22, by installing without the platform addon packages and asserting artifact() is wasm; macOS, Windows, other Node lines and other causes of the fallback are core-supported and not qualified here

unqualified.host: macOS x64, Linux arm64 and musl, Windows arm64, and Node 20 and 22 on macOS and Windows
unqualified.how: the per-platform clean-tarball smoke runs on macOS (arm64 runner) and Windows (x64 runner), Node 24, native addon only; the core supports more platforms and owns that matrix

adapter-ai-context is the only package intended for a browser bundle, qualified by npm run smoke-test:browser (esbuild, run on Node's WebAssembly engine); real browsers, Vite, webpack, Rollup, Workers, Deno, Bun and SSR builds are unqualified, and every other package is Node-only
peerDependencies ^0.1.0-beta.6 on every npm package: npm 7 and later stop with ERESOLVE

optional peerDependency >=1.26.0 <=1.32.1 on adapter-mcp: when the SDK is installed, npm 7 and later stop with ERESOLVE on a version outside it unless --legacy-peer-deps or --force overrides it. The cap is the highest tested release: a newer one is unqualified until it is added as an endpoint here. The floor is 1.26.0, the first release clear of the high-severity advisories GHSA-w48q-cv73-mx4w, GHSA-8r9q-7v3j-jr4g and GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7: an older SDK is refused rather than qualified with them (#83)
optional peerDependencies >=2.0.0 <=2.3.1 on adapter-mcp: npm 7 and later stop with ERESOLVE on a version outside it unless --legacy-peer-deps or --force overrides it
the otel extra requires opentelemetry-sdk>=1.16.0,<2: pip's resolver refuses a conflicting pin (checked 2026-09-25 with pip 26.2.1 and opentelemetry-sdk==1.15.0)
dependency redact-secret>=0.1.0b6,<0.2: pip's resolver refuses a conflicting pin
requires-python >=3.10: pip finds no installable distribution (checked 2026-09-25 for 3.9)
requires-python has no upper bound, so pip installs it; 3.15 and later are not exercised by CI and are unqualified
engines is advisory: npm only warns unless engine-strict is set, so an install succeeds; those runtimes are not exercised by CI and are unqualified

unqualified.host: OpenTelemetry string-array attribute width (JavaScript and Python span processors)
unqualified.how: the span processors apply maxStringLength per element but no element-count bound of their own to a string-array attribute; the SDK's attribute limits are the only bound, so a very wide array costs one scan per element
